The '''HT drone''' were small semi-spherical drones which complemented the larger [[RHTC-560 Hunter Trainer]]s. They were used by the Master Controllers as scouts to track and eliminate prey during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]]. The [[RHTC-560 Hunter Trainer|RHTC-560 system]] was developed by [[Rodian D-Tec]].

==Description==
In stark contrast to the towering controller units, the HT drones were small circular droids about half the size of an [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech droid]]. Each drone came with two forward retractable arms for manipulating objects and two hind legs. 
When not using their four limbs for traversing over the jungle floor, the used their [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] unit for hovering over their targets. To simulate armed confrontation, they were equipped with [[Stun blaster/Legends|stun blasters]].<ref name="guide">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref>

As with most other simpler droid designs, these drones lacked independent personal programming and were entirely controlled by their 560 control unit, which decided the tactics and their movements. The 560 could control up to ten drones within a range of 50 km, challenging trainees in coordinated and cooperating adversaries.<ref name="guide" /> Distance impaired their effectiveness in long-range hunts. However, this was compensated by the RHTC-560 system's creativity subroutine which allowed it to remain operational even in a wide range of tricky situations. Even if the control unit was submerged underwater, it was still able to command its associated drone units.

For operations in the dark of night or the depths of a jungle, these drones were equipped with [[hi-intensity searchlight]]s to locate their prey. 

==Operational history==
The RHTC-560 Hunter Trainer system was originally marketed locally by [[Rodian D-Tec]] on the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]] to suit the native Rodian appetite for violence and combat. Their customers ranged from bounty hunters to the various Rodian clans which used them in both their [[Rodian Clan Wars|clan wars]] and hunts to even the dictatorial [[Grand Protector/Legends|Grand Protector]] [[Navik/Legends|Navik the Red]]. It is alleged that the Grand Protector's RHTC-560 system had been modified with lethal [[Disruptor/Legends|disruptor]] cannons for used against his captives in competitions.

Throughout the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]], their popularity was sufficient enough for the series to be marketed offworld beyond the confines of Rodia. With 2,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for each HT drone and another 5,000 credits for each control unit, the series was economical enough for many non-Rodian [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] as well as local plantetary militias and police academies. Three were also given to the [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of the ''[[Anya Karu]]'', [[Aron Harcourt]]. They would later fight, and lose to, the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].
